notes: §1985:XI.4.4.4 GR6 orders the SORT into three phases: records made available by RELEASE in the input procedure or implicit READs of file-name-2, which 'must not be in the open mode' when the phase commences and 'is not in the open mode' when it ends; sequencing with no processing of file-name-2 or file-name-3; then the sorted records written to file-name-3 or RETURNed to the output procedure, with the same open-mode statements for file-name-3. SortEmitter.EmitSort emits exactly that order with no edition arm: phase a (EmitInputFile plus each file's implicit CLOSE, or the input procedure), phase b (SortSort, SortWork.Sequence), phase c (EmitGivingFile or the output procedure), and CobolSort.FileNotOpen before each phase (the 2023 EC-SORT-MERGE-FILE-OPEN test, which below 2023 only nets a violation 1985 leaves undefined). Probes at 85 (work-slice-46/c6): e) phases, USING a sequential, a relative and an indexed file with an output procedure that OPENs and READs two of the USING files (S1=00 CCC, S3=00, so they were closed after phase a), then RET AAA BBB CCC DDD; USING F1 GIVING F1 rewrites F1 in sorted order (CCC AAA); openatstart, a missing USING file runs its USE procedure (35) and a USING file already open gives 41 (undefined at 85, so either result conforms); c4/givafter (case 12) shows file-name-3 opened only after the input procedure. Witness: USING/GIVING then OPEN of both files prints AAA BBB CCC DONE.

next.reason: Same three phases. 1985 says file-name-2/file-name-3 'must not be in the open mode' when the phase commences and states no outcome. §2023:14.9.40.4 GR9 instead defines one: 'the EC-SORT-MERGE-FILE-OPEN exception condition is set to exist and the results of the execution of the SORT statement are undefined'. An unstated violation became a defined exception condition (PB5008 mode c).
